title: POC Ops Handoff & Quantization Tuning - Weekly Sync
summary: Weekly POC sync focusing on access handoff, environment readiness, and initial quantization tuning. Agreed testing plan for latency/cost tradeoffs and next steps for security docs and benchmark run. Noted a credentials snag for staging gateway and a request to try 4-bit quant profiles vs 8-bit for cost/latency evaluation.
action_items: Jordan Lee: share SOC2 + network diagram + RedTeam checklist; due 2026-05-22
Maya Patel: spin up two benchmark variants (8-bit baseline, 4-bit quantized) and share results; due 2026-05-26
Priya Shah: confirm firewall egress rules and provide staging gateway IP allowlist; due 2026-05-21
Alex Gomez: validate that the service account has KMS decrypt permissions in staging; due 2026-05-21
Liam O'Connor: schedule deep-dive on rollout/fallback policies with product + infra; propose times by 2026-05-20
next_steps: Run 10k-req synthetic benchmark with two quant profiles and 95th percentile latency capture
Redwood to provide security packet and architecture diagram
Customer to finish allowlist and KMS perms so Redwood can run in-staging trials
Follow-up deep-dive meeting for canary/rollback logic next week
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (AE): ok hey everybody thanks for joining, um we'll kick off. this is the bluecove weekly poc sync - ops handoff and a quick tuning pass on quantization. quick roll call? 
[00:10] Alex (CTO): alex here. 
[00:12] Priya (SRE): priya here. 
[00:14] Tom (Product): tom - hey. 
[00:16] Maya (SE): maya with redwood. 
[00:18] Heather (Security): heather here. 
[00:22] Jordan: cool. real quick agenda: creds & gateway state, staging readiness, benchmark plan (we'll test 8-bit baseline then 4-bit quant), and security items. any additions? 
[00:35] Priya: oh yeah one blocker — the staging gateway was returning 403 on the redwood service account last night, we need the allowlist updated. 
[00:40] Jordan: ok that's the credential snag we flagged last week, priya can you confirm the rule we need? 
[00:45] Priya: yeah. we need egress to 52.23.14.0/24 and the service account needs KMS decrypt on the staging key. also current proxy is doing TLS termination so we want to check cert chain. 
[00:58] Maya: got it. once we have allowlist + KMS perms we can kick off in-staging load tests. i'll also try a fallback to hosted if staging capacity throttles. 
[01:10] Tom: timeline wise if we get perms in next 48 hours we can review results on thursday. is that realistic? 
[01:18] Jordan: yes, we can run the benchmark and share a writeup. maya, you'll run two variants right? 
[01:23] Maya: correct. baseline is the current 8-bit quant profile on the optimized runtime, and then 4-bit low-precision quant to see cost delta and latency changes. note that 4-bit sometimes shows worse tail latency depending on batch shapes here. also we need to watch kv cache warmup — initial requests will pay the warmup cost. 
[01:40] Alex: is that the key-value cache, is it K V cash in the transcript? we saw some warmup spikes in our own tests. 
[01:46] Maya: yep KV cache — some transcripts say K V cash lol — it holds keys for longer sequences, so the first few calls have higher CPU/GPU. we can instrument to report cache hit rate. 
[01:58] Heather (Security): quick sec: can you confirm where logs live, retention and whether any PII could be stored in logs during the pilot? our compliance needs to know. 
[02:06] Jordan: good question. by default we redact prompts that are marked PII and logs go to the customer-controlled storage in the private deployment— for hosted we retain minimal telemetry, we will include the retention windows in the packet. 
[02:18] Heather: ok we need SOC2 section and network diagram. 
[02:21] Jordan: i'll send the security packet after this meeting. 
[02:25] Priya: another question: we plan to run a 95th percentile SLO of 250ms for short prompts (<= 128 tokens). is that achievable on your dedicated slices? 
[02:34] Maya: short answer: yes on dedicated with tuned batch sizing and prefix caching; on hosted it depends on region and load. for the pilot we'll benchmark both flavors. for 4-bit quant we might see avg token latency drop but tail could be slightly higher — depends on kernel selection and kernel fallback. 
[02:54] Alex: what about cost tradeoffs — do you have an estimate for tokens/sec per GPU on 4-bit vs 8-bit? 
[03:03] Maya: we have rough unit economics: 4-bit can reduce memory and cost by ~30-40% for some models but it's model and sequence dependent. we'll include per-token cost estimates in the benchmark artifact. 
[03:16] Tom: are we planning canary strategies if we roll quantized models to production? 
[03:20] Liam (CSM): yes we recommend canary by user cohort and auto-rollback on quality regressions tied to eval sets. we'll run a canary playbook with you in the rollout deep-dive. 
[03:32] Alex: on quality regressions — do you do eval hooks or do we run offline evals? we want to avoid hallucination spikes. 
[03:39] Maya: both. we support eval hooks tied to prompt sets and offline evals. in-pipeline quality monitors can trigger rollback. we'll need your eval prompts to avoid false positives. 
[03:50] Heather: KMS question — is customer-managed keys supported on staging? we've been told yes but need confirmation. 
[03:55] Jordan: yes customer-managed KMS is supported for private deployments and staging can be configured to use your key, we'll document the exact IAM bindings needed. 
[04:04] Priya: note: our cert chain has an intermediate that some clients choke on, so we might need to rotate certs if redwood's client rejects it. 
[04:12] Maya: if that happens we can use the hosted fallback to avoid blocking tests. 
[04:18] Alex: what's next week look like — when can we get the deep-dive? 
[04:22] Jordan: liam will coordinate times; we aim for a 60–90 minute session focused on rollback/canary and SLO enforcement. liam, can you take that? 
[04:30] Liam: yep i'll send Doodle options today. 
[04:32] [crosstalk] 
[04:35] Maya: quick detail on benchmarks: we'll run 10k synthetic requests, capture p50/p95/p99, memory, GPU utilization, and kv hit rate. please note that early runs will show the cold-kv penalty. 
[04:48] Priya: we'll try to seed the KV cache by replaying representative sessions before the measurement window. 
[04:52] Jordan: perfect. 
[04:55] Tom: any blockers for the customer's side other than allowlist + KMS? 
[04:59] Priya: also need the staging service account to be created with the right roles, i'm finalizing that after this call. 
[05:05] Heather: and a short security questionnaire — will redwood complete your vendor security form or do we need to fill something out? 
[05:12] Jordan: we can fill your form; also we will provide our packet for information. either way works, we'll coordinate. 
[05:18] Alex: can you also include the model verification steps so our product folks can see quality checks? 
[05:22] Maya: yes we'll include the eval harness and example alerts. 
[05:26] Jordan: ok let's do a short recap and next steps. recap: redwood to send security + network diagrams, maya to run the two benchmark variants and share artifacts, priya to finalize allowlist & KMS perms. liam to schedule deep-dive. 
[05:40] Alex: sounds good. 
[05:42] Jordan: anything else? 
[05:44] Speaker 6: random note — competitor x was mentioned earlier, we tried them and saw 30% cost but higher latency. 
[05:51] Jordan: ok thanks. we'll follow up by EOD with the packet and timeline. thanks everyone. meeting adjourned.
[05:58] [end of recording]
